chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no objection to buying the Ajam (uncertain/indeterminate goods) if there is Qasab (a known quantity/measure) in them."

key_terms.اَلْآجَامَ: Uncertain or indeterminate goods (plural of Ajam)
key_terms.قَصَبٌ: A known quantity, measure, or standard portion
key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ: There is no objection / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for buying uncertain goods (Ajam) to be permissible in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify that the prohibition of *gharar* (excessive uncertainty) in trade is lifted when a known, measurable standard (*Qasab*) exists within the bulk goods. This principle allows for the sale of commodities like grain or fruit where the exact total quantity is unknown, provided a representative sample or portion is clearly defined, thereby ensuring fairness and preventing dispute in commercial transactions.
